title: Ride-sharing legalised with taxi reform package (SA)
summary: South Australia legalised ride-sharing from 1 July 2016 as part of a taxi and chauffeur industry reform, with taxi licence compensation funded by a per-trip levy and taxis keeping rank-and-hail exclusivity.

instruments.title: Passenger Transport Variation Regulations 2016
instruments.provisions: In operation 1 Jul 2016; mainly taxi provisions

instruments.title: Passenger Transport (Point to Point Transport Services) Variation Regulations 2017
instruments.provisions: Defines chauffeured vehicle and taxi services

commenced.what: Ride-sharing permitted to operate legally (accredited drivers/vehicles)

direction_rationale: Legalising app-based ride-share removes the legal barrier to entry created by taxi/hire-car licence quotas, adding a new type of supplier and price competition in point-to-point transport.
comparison: States that had not yet legalised ride-sharing (ACT Oct 2015 first, NT Dec 2017/Feb 2018 last)
confounders: taxi licence compensation and per-trip levies
ABN registration by gig drivers inflates business counts

verified.notes: Announcement and 1 Jul 2016 legal start are from news reports (InDaily); the official instrument that legalised ride-share was not confirmed.
